title: Sales Enablement: Prospect Playbook - Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Avery Kim
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips GTM and SDR teams with concise positioning, competitive talking points, sample pitch-deck guidance, pricing guardrails, short case studies, and an up-to-date Security FAQ for prospect conversations. Use this as the canonical single-page reference during discovery and qualification.

Target audience: SDRs, AEs, presales, solutions engineering, and channel partners.

Quick elevator (30s): Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, low-latency, and cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments - so engineering teams can ship LLM features without building inference ops.

1) Positioning & Messaging

Primary value props (use in order based on prospect need):
- Production economics: Reduce per-token cost and operational overhead using intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and model/quantization recommendations.
- Predictable performance: SLA-backed Dedicated capacity and observable SLOs in Redwood Console for latency and throughput.
- Deployment flexibility: One API and control plane across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated workloads.
- Developer experience: Simple REST/SDKs, streaming, tool/function calling, and ready quickstarts to accelerate time-to-value.

Messaging frameworks (choose by persona):
- Engineering lead: "Ship safely and predictably - same API across environments, deterministic latency, and tooling to keep unit economics under control."
- Platform owner: "Standardize LLM serving across product teams while controlling cost and enforcing security boundaries (Dedicated & Private)."
- Security/compliance buyer: "Private deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and fine-grained RBAC satisfy enterprise compliance requirements."

Key objections and responses:
- Objection: "We can self-host cheaper."
  Response: "Maybe at peak scale, but Redwood reduces development and ops cost: optimized kernels, autoscaling, and continuous batching deliver lower total cost of ownership and faster time-to-market."
- Objection: "We need strict data residency."
  Response: "Private deployment supports VPC/on-prem with retention controls and configurable audit logs. We have reference architectures and compliance evidence for common frameworks (SOC2, ISO)."

2) Competitive Briefs (high-level)

Competitor: Large Cloud Provider Managed Endpoints
- Differentiators: Redwood focuses on inference economics and developer experience specifically for LLMs (automatic batching, quantization recommendations, model catalog with verified perf profiles). More prescriptive cost/perf levers and cross-environment consistency.

Competitor: LLM API provider X (ease-of-use focused)
- Differentiators: Comparable developer ergonomics, but Redwood emphasizes performance observability, Dedicated capacity SLAs, and private deployment options for regulated customers.

Competitor: Self-hosted inference runtimes (open-source)
- Differentiators: Redwood offers a managed orchestration, autoscaling, and continuous operational tooling (tracing, token-level cost breakdown, rollout automation) that avoids long-term maintenance burden.

Competitive positioning bullets for discovery call:
- "If your priority is predictable latency and cost at scale, we provide SLA-backed Dedicated and automated fallback policies to keep apps healthy under load."
- "If you have compliance needs, our Private deployment and audit tools reduce blocker friction for procurement."

3) Pitch Deck Guidance (recommended slides and callouts)

Required deck sections (5-8 slides recommended for discovery):
- Cover: Logo, one-line value prop, persona-focused subheadline.
- Problem (1 slide): Rising inference costs, unpredictable latency, fragmentation across environments. Use customer metrics: e.g., 2-3x token cost variance without batching.
- Solution (1-2 slides): Redwood platform overview - Hosted API, Dedicated, Private; mention runtime optimizations and Redwood Console.
- Differentiation (1 slide): Bullet areas - performance SLOs, cost controls (batching/quantization), unified API, security.
- Customer proof (1 slide): Quick case study metrics (see below).
- Pricing & next steps (1 slide): Tailored pricing pathway, trial details, SE workshop offer.

Deck callouts for SEs and AEs:
- Use consistent customer metrics (latency, cost per 1k tokens, throughput) when available.
- Call out model variants and quantization options if prospect cares about on-prem memory footprint.
- Always end with a clear next step: trial, pilot, or technical deep-dive.

4) Pricing Guidance (discovery-level; always confirm with finance)

Standard hosted pricing (example guidance to prospects; all numbers illustrative):
- Text generation: $0.003 per 1k input tokens / $0.012 per 1k output tokens for base models (discounts for committed usage).
- Embeddings: $0.0004 per vector call (1K-dim baseline) with volume tiers.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Monthly commitments start at $Xk/month (tailor per GPU type and throughput).
- Private: Platform license + deployment engineering fee; typical enterprise engagements include a setup/validation milestone.

Quote process and guardrails:
- Small POCs (<$10k ARR): recommend Hosted trial credits + SE workshop.
- Mid-market pilots ($10k- $100k ARR): propose short-term Dedicated bursts or hosted with committed discount.
- Enterprise (>$100k ARR): engage Sales Engineering + Finance for dedicated contract (include SLA terms).

Common pricing objections and guidance:
- If prospect asks for per-call limits or predictable monthly cost, propose Dedicated with committed throughput and a monthly capped plan.
- For procurement: provide example T&C templates and an estimated cost model based on expected tokens/day.

5) Case Studies (short, use in deck and emails)

Case Study - Conversational Support Platform (mid-market)
- Situation: Support vendor saw escalating token costs and inconsistent latency across regions.
- Outcome: After migrating to Redwood Dedicated + prefix caching, they reduced per-token spend by 35% and improved median latency from 220ms to 120ms.
- Asset: One-page PDF with before/after charts (link in assets library).

Case Study - Regulated Financial Platform (enterprise)
- Situation: Required VPC-only deployment with strict KMS controls and audit logging.
- Outcome: Deployed Redwood Private with KMS/HSM integration and passed security review; pilot scaled to production within 12 weeks.
- Asset: Customer testimonial quote and referenceable contact (with legal approval).

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers; expand with Security team for sensitive requests)

Q: Does Redwood store customer prompts or outputs?
A: By default, Hosted logs minimal metadata for observability; customers can opt out of data retention. Dedicated and Private deployments can be configured to avoid persistent storage and route logs to customer-managed sinks.

Q: What encryption is used for data in transit and at rest?
A: TLS 1.2+ for transit; AES-256 for at-rest on managed services. For Private deployments, customers control KMS/HSM.

Q: Can we bring our own key management (BYOK)?
A: Yes - Dedicated and Private support KMS integrations and HSM-backed keys for private key storage.

Q: Which compliance frameworks do you support?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and is pursuing ISO 27001. For regulated customers we provide compliance evidence packages and a reference architecture for data residency.

Q: How do you isolate tenant workloads on Dedicated?
A: Dedicated uses isolated GPU pools with network segmentation and RBAC at the control plane; per-customer auditing and token-level cost reporting are provided.

Q: What is your incident response and notification SLA?
A: See our Incident Response playbook; critical incidents notify customers via email/slack within 15 minutes and a postmortem within 72 hours for severity-1 events.

7) Sales Play (recommended steps)

1. Discovery: Use the positioning bullets and 3-5 priority questions (workload, throughput, latency targets, compliance needs, budget).
2. Qualify: Map needs to Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; capture expected tokens/day and SLO requirements.
3. Demo/SE workshop: Offer a 2-3 hour technical workshop showing integration, simple perf test, and cost model.
4. Trial/Pilot: Enroll in Hosted trial or short Dedicated burst; provide clear success criteria (latency, cost savings, throughput).
5. Contracting: Engage legal/procurement early for Private or Dedicated, and use our procurement checklist.
